# The required status checks on the `main` ruleset, and how each one is run.
#
# Left of `=` is the status-check context, exactly as the ruleset names it.
# Right of `=` is one of:
#
#   just <recipe>   the job runs exactly this recipe, so local and CI cannot
#                   diverge — the workflow contains no copy of the command
#   partial: <why>  a recipe of that name exists but the job does more, because
#                   part of the check needs something only GitHub has
#   github-only:    no recipe can exist
#
# crates/repo-conformance asserts all of that against the workflows and the
# justfile, offline. `just brief` asserts that this file still matches the live
# ruleset, which needs a token and so cannot run in CI's pull-request context.
# Neither half is sufficient alone.
#
# Adding a required check means adding it in three places — the ruleset, a
# workflow job, and here. That is the cost of the guarantee; ADR 0017 states it.

build             = just build
tests             = just tests
lint              = just lint
fmt               = just fmt
msrv              = just msrv
platforms         = just platforms
schema-validation = just schema-validation
cargo-deny        = just cargo-deny
licence-headers   = just licence-headers
dco               = just dco
mutants           = just mutants
workflow-audit    = partial: the recipe runs zizmor and the structural rules; the job runs zizmor through its action so findings upload as SARIF
gate              = partial: the recipe reports what the base revision's policy demands; collecting evidence from check runs, and deriving the actor's tier, exist only on GitHub
analyze (rust)    = github-only: CodeQL runs on GitHub's analysis infrastructure
analyze (actions) = github-only: CodeQL runs on GitHub's analysis infrastructure
